title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 314: Space and Mind: Architecture & Brain
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 314 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

Space and Mind: The Cognitive Ergonomics of Architecture

Paragraph 1. For more than a century, modern architecture followed Louis Sullivan's famous rule: 'form follows function.' Designers treated buildings mainly as practical containers judged by structural strength, heating, and fire safety. However, in Mind in Architecture, cognitive scientist Dr. Colin Ellard shows that this narrow view misses an essential truth: our built surroundings continuously alter human brain activity, hormone levels, and mental health.

Paragraph 2. Ellard's research field—neuro-architecture—uses body sensors, virtual reality, and brain scans to measure how physical spaces shape thinking. One key discovery concerns ceiling height, known as the 'Cathedral Effect.' In laboratory trials, volunteers placed in rooms with high ceilings (three metres or above) solved creative, big-picture tasks much more effectively. Conversely, people working inside rooms with low ceilings paid closer attention to small details and careful step-by-step calculations.

Paragraph 3. Street-level building walls have an equally powerful effect on the human mind. In walking experiments across New York, Berlin, and London, Ellard fitted volunteers with skin sensors and eye-tracking glasses. When pedestrians passed long, unbroken glass fronts or blank concrete walls, their heart rates slowed and skin tests showed deep boredom alongside higher stress hormones. By contrast, lively historic streets with varied textures and frequent doorways activated brain areas linked to curiosity and enjoyment.

Paragraph 4. Ellard warns that for decades, city builders have chosen cheap, identical glass towers that starve human senses. By ignoring how space affects psychology, planners accidentally create lonely, stressed urban communities. Buildings are never silent scenery; they actively shape how people think and feel together.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...alter human brain activity, hormone levels, and mental health."

q6.text: The buildings we spend time in can influence hormone levels in our bodies.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...continuously alter human brain activity, hormone levels..."

q7.text: Rooms with high ceilings improve performance on careful step-by-step calculations.

steps: Đoạn 2: Trần cao tốt cho tư duy sáng tạo; trần thấp mới phục vụ tính toán từng bước chi tiết.

q8.text: Commercial developers regularly hire neuroscientists before designing glass towers.

steps: Đoạn 4: Chỉ nói nhà phát triển chọn tháp kính rẻ tiền, không nhắc họ có thuê nhà thần kinh học hay không.

q9.text: Walking past blank concrete walls made pedestrians feel excited and energetic.

steps: Đoạn 3: Người đi bộ cảm thấy chán nản sâu sắc và căng thẳng hơn, không phải hào hứng.

q10.text: Standardized glass buildings can contribute to loneliness and stress in cities.
